label: MiniMax M3.1 Flash
output:
Here's the letter — 24 copies, one per door. Written in first person, no finger-pointing, and it leaves the note's author unnamed.

---

Dear Larkspur Lofts residents,

I'm writing to everyone about the drone flight on Saturday, October 31, and to offer an explanation and an apology, since a note in the lobby made clear that some of you were unsettled by what you saw.

I've lived in 5A for three years. That afternoon I took a short test flight of a new drone, a Halvard Mini 4, in preparation for a wedding shoot in Dundee. The flight lasted about eleven minutes, ending shortly after 4:00 p.m. The camera was pointed west the entire time, toward the Willamette River and the Fremont Bridge. It was never aimed at windows, balconies, or the courtyard, and no images of residents or of any interior were captured. I have the complete, unedited footage and am glad to show it to anyone who would like to see it. You can knock on the door of 5A at any time, or write to me at jess.okafor@mailbox.example.

That said, I don't want to lean on where the camera was pointing. A small buzzing aircraft hanging over a courtyard is genuinely unsettling if you don't know what it is, and I understand why it looked like something worse. I'm sorry it worried people. I'm grateful to Doreen in 2C, who was kind enough to tell me her grandchildren were frightened by the sight of it; she came to me directly, and I appreciated that.

I also want to say, plainly, that being identified in a public note, with my unit number on it, was hurtful. Singling out one resident that way in a space everyone walks through feels different from a word to a neighbor at the mailboxes, and I'd rather not have it repeated. If something I do concerns you, please come to me directly. I will always listen, and I'd much rather hear it in a hallway conversation than read it on a sheet of tape.

As far as I know, there is currently no HOA rule addressing drones. So that this doesn't have to be settled by private judgment, I won't fly from the roof deck again until the board has had the chance to decide on a policy, and I'd ask that drone use be added to the agenda for the board meeting on November 19 at 7:00 p.m. in the community room. My own preference is to leave the roof deck off limits entirely, but I'd rather the question be resolved openly and for everyone.

Thank you for reading this, and for living here. I look forward to seeing many of you on the 19th.

Sincerely,
Jess Okafor
Unit 5A

---

Two small notes: it comes to about 380 words, and you can cut the Doreen paragraph entirely if you'd rather not make her the source publicly — it won't leave any obvious gap.
